tools/lint_levels.py now exits zero over all 1208 levels (was 37 problems in 37 levels). Every fix is in a generator, and all three generators are idempotent: running level_templates.py, level_gen.py and target_gen.py back to back leaves the tree byte-for-byte unchanged, so the fixes survive regeneration.

Three faults, all traced to four kit templates (15, 28, 35, 69/94):
1. 12 levels carried a COLLECT target for colour 4 under COLOR LIMIT 4. Item.GenItem rolls Random.Range(0, colorLimit), so that item never spawned and the level was unwinnable. level_gen.scale_colours now floors the limit at one past the highest colour any inherited COLLECT target names; level_templates.py harvests those colours from the template's target asset.
2. 23 levels were MODE 3 with a BLOCKS target of 0 — Done() on load, so a blocks level was won without touching a block and the HUD drew a chip that ticked itself on frame one. target_gen.repair_dead_targets fills it from the board.
3. 2 levels carried a second INGREDIENT target at 0 — a dead HUD chip, and Item.GenItem iterates every ingredient target, so it started a second FallingCor for every gem the board spawned. The dead entry is now dropped.

Added tools/shipped_targets/ — pristine copies of the kit's 100 target assets, the sibling of tools/shipped_levels/. The generators read templates from there and never from Resources/Targets, which holds their own output; sourcing from Resources is what would have made a second run differ from the first.

- 12 levels go from 4 colours to 5: 136, 155, 201, 206, 237, 315, 323, 337, 344, 350, 523, 524. Harder, and the only value that makes their goal reachable at all.

The 18-block boards land at 0.72-0.86 blocks/move; the all-double-block boards are capped at exactly 3.00.
- 2 levels lose a dead ingredient chip: 15 and 105. Difficulty unchanged — the entry was already met on load.
- No other level's target count moved. The 447 levels with a non-zero blocks target were left alone.
